## Resolved

| Decision | Status | Chosen/leaning | Alternatives | Source | Date |

| repair-lock guarantee statement (roll 13, third window class → re-charter) | resolved | The `.dev/node-modules-repair.lock` guarantee this item ships is **best-effort serialization plus result-fencing of the displaced side**: a displaced holder's result is never trusted (the exit fence added at fd57356). It does NOT provide mutual exclusion against an alive-past-expiry holder — a fixed-expiry advisory file lock with steal cannot; the roll-13 survivor (seat-deps-core.js:422: a stalled-but-alive holder may still execute while its successor's fenced result is trusted) is that residual, the third distinct window class in this protocol after slot-mutation syscalls (rolls 5–11, adjudicated) and reclamation displacement/restore (roll 12, fixed). That residual is chartered as #761 (liveness-aware exclusion protocol, shared primitive with file-lock.ts, format-pinning conformance test) and is not a claim of this PR. The claim under review is the narrowed guarantee above. | rebuild the exclusion primitive under this gate (new mechanism under a red gate; barred by operator policy) | PR #699 roll-13 review comment (codex standard survivor at seat-deps-core.js:422); issue #761 | 2026-09-01 |
| repair-path TOCTOU findings (rolls 5–11 re-found one class: check-then-mutate windows in the managed-slot repair sequence — lstat→unlink, unlink→symlink, restore-rename; roll 16 re-found the same premise as a detection gap: an in-store decoy symlink vs lexical `linkIsHealthy`) | resolved | Operator adjudication, made with the operator after reading all recorded gate rolls, verbatim: "repair is never the trust point — the point-of-use verify inside the exclusion primitive (.dev/node-modules-repair.lock, which seat provisioning already takes at worktree-deps.ts:612) is. Adversarial seat interleaving during repair is out of the gate's authority, because a seat that can Bash-write MAIN doesn't need the race — it can corrupt after repair too." No further per-syscall race patching on the repair path; the write fence for seats is #262/#573's acceptance surface. The same boundary covers roll 16's decoy-symlink finding (seat-deps-core.js `linkIsHealthy`): a decoy intermediate symlink inside MAIN's store exists only if a seat wrote MAIN's shared node_modules — #262/#573's acceptance surface again, not this item's. Literal-link health is the operator's roll-9 re-scope choice; realpath-equality was rejected as the health basis because a seat store can legitimately resolve into MAIN's store (pinned by the seat-relative-target test in authoring-review-seat.test.ts). | keep patching each next syscall window per roll (rolls 9–11 each did once; each patch surfaced the next window); switch health to realpath-equality (rejected in the roll-9 re-scope — spoofable by a seat store resolving into MAIN's store) | PR #699 gate rolls 5–11 and 16 (upserted review comment; roll-11 survivors at seat-deps-core.js:349, roll-16 survivor at seat-deps-core.js:322) | 2026-08-31 (extended 2026-09-01) |
